# Critical Momentum-Transfer Questions {#sec-critical-momentum-questions}

The model ladder now permits bounded answers to several recurring questions,
but it does not support a single transfer percentage, a universal release
time, or a preferred human technique. @tbl-momentum-question-status
separates present results from the observations needed to change them. The
prospective experiment definitions are machine-readable in
[`momentum_transfer_experiment_registry.json`](../data/momentum_transfer_experiment_registry.json),
and their broader rationale is documented in the open
[`question program`](../MOMENTUM_TRANSFER_QUESTION_PROGRAM.md).

| Question | Present Assessment | What Would Change the Assessment? |
|---|---|---|
| How much transfer is drift-mediated? | Conditional on the observable, coordinate and frame, event window, model, and decomposition. Signed drift shares may exceed 100% when control opposes the pathway; pointwise attribution is not forward persistence. | A common acceleration/force/impulse/power/work ledger across tiers, same-state killswitches, uncertainty propagation, and participant-held-out bilateral-wrench evaluation. |
| Which geometry matters? | Relative link angle, force direction, velocity direction, reference point, grip separation, swing-plane orientation, and contact moment arm can gate magnitude and sign. | A subject-scaled spatial atlas with zero, orthogonal, coincident-grip, and reversed-moment-arm controls reproduced in an independent engine. |
| Which timing patterns matter? | Early distal release changes the available geometry; proximal rate, acceleration, braking, and release timing interact nonmonotonically. “Casting” is not one universal event. | Factorial interventions on proximal acceleration, distal release, and braking under matched state and work, with multiple preregistered casting definitions and adverse-load tests. |
| Does a drift-mediated strategy require less timing precision? | Unresolved for people. State triggering improves selected synthetic outcomes but assumes state access and does not prove reduced neural timing demand. | Clock, state, impedance, and delayed-observer policies compared by viable timing-region volume, lower-tail outcome, phase error, delay, saturation, force, and effort. |
| Is a strategy self-correcting? | Not established. Low perturbation sensitivity is not self-correction without a recovery mechanism. | Matched perturbations demonstrating error decay, recovery time, viable-set return probability, attraction-region size, and no hidden load-cost increase. |
| Should proximal velocity be maximized? | No general rule is supported. The reduced studies contain phase dependence, matching-rule dependence, nonmonotonic killswitch effects, and adverse braking associations. | Dose-response surfaces for rate and acceleration with matched state, work, load, and impact definitions, extended across spatial and subject-scaled models and held-out participants. |
| Is slack beneficial or necessary? | Unanswered until the mechanism is named. Contact loss, backlash, elastic preload, muscle-tendon series compliance, and control deadband are not interchangeable. | One slack class at a time, with a state and constitutive law, matched initial energy, passivity and closure checks, hysteresis sweeps, and a measurement strategy. |

## Timing and Common Failure Descriptions

The terms *casting*, *weak early body acceleration*, and *late release* are
useful only after translation into observables. The registered timing study
therefore treats at least four quantities independently: proximal-acceleration
onset, distal-angle or distal-rate threshold crossing, proximal-braking onset,
and the impact or delivery event. A result is not robust if it depends on one
arbitrary casting threshold. Work-matched and delivery-state-matched controls
are both required because either matching rule can alter the apparent benefit.

## Timing Demand and Self-Correction

A mechanism can be mechanically passive at an instant while its preparation
or regulation remains demanding. Timing demand is therefore reported as the
width or volume of a viable event-time region, outcome sensitivity to phase
error, lower-tail performance, and degradation under observer delay and
noise. Self-correction has the stronger requirement that a declared physical
or feedback mechanism return a perturbed state toward a viable set. Repeatable
open-loop behavior does not meet that definition.

## Proximal Velocity as a Dose, Not a Maxim

The existing planar evidence is sufficient to reject the rule “maximize
proximal velocity” at those declared tiers, but not to specify a human optimum.
An apparent speed benefit must be considered together with relative motion,
control work, interface power, braking work, bilateral load, club orientation,
and the matching rule. The registered analysis searches explicitly for
plateaus, interior optima, and reversals rather than forcing a monotonic fit.

## Five Distinct Slack Hypotheses

1. **Contact slack** is temporary loss or weakening of a hand-grip constraint.
2. **Transmission slack** is backlash or a dead zone before torque transmission.
3. **Structural slack** is compliant preload and elastic deformation.
4. **Biological series compliance** is a muscle-tendon state with stored and
   released energy.
5. **Control slack** is an activation deadband, delay, or co-contraction reserve.

Only the declared phenomenological transmission dead zone has been exercised
directly in the present allocation study. The other classes remain separate
experiments. Any proposed benefit must survive matched-energy, zero-slack,
direction-reversal, passivity, and work-energy closure controls before it can
be interpreted as a transfer mechanism.

## Evidential Boundary

These experiments are designed to make the framework easier to disprove.
Synthetic studies can reject a mechanism within a declared model and can
qualify software, but they cannot establish a coaching instruction or human
control strategy. The participant-held-out stage remains blocked until a
governed dataset contains synchronized full-body and club kinematics, force
plates, bilateral six-axis grip wrenches, grip/contact state, and impact
outcomes. Substituting synthetic traces would erase the question the human
stage is intended to answer.
